<result>Both tasks are merged to main and completed, and both bugs are closed. For each item I did the full loop: claim, a regression test that failed first, gates, merge, complete. The reviewers were the LAN DeepSeek. I also ran roborev for the standards gate.

**fix-B71c3bcda14** (merged as cb1dc0ff)
- **Fix:** `tests/_isolation.py::_updating` now reads syrupy's `update_snapshots` option instead of `snapshot_update`, so the guard recognises a `--snapshot-update` session.
- **Regression test:** `tests/test_isolation_snapshot_update.py::test_guard_sees_syrupy_update_session`.
- **CI:** the ci gate ran the full suite and passed.

**fix-B76f42d8f1f** (merged as 16a87581)
- **Cause:** the heuristic was not word-guessing. `_file_fix_task` copied the whole glob list of the item the bug was found on.
- **Fix:** I added `inherit_globs` in `ddflow/services/bug_globs.py`, called from `ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py`. If the bug text names files, the fix task keeps only the source globs those files match, which can be none.
- **Case from the bug:** with the real summary and `DX-claim-agent-flag-adoption`'s globs, the function now returns an empty list, because the summary names `README.md`.
- **Regression test:** `tests/test_bug_globs_heuristic.py::test_bug_found_does_not_copy_unrelated_globs`, plus unit tests for the helper.
- **Review rounds:** reviewers and roborev found real problems and I fixed them:
  - slash-words like `read/write` and `50/50.` were read as file names;
  - the same basename in another directory matched;
  - a swapped `fnmatch` argument broke wildcard-basename globs.
- **Forced rounds:** the rubber_duck gate went past its round budget with two `--force --reason` rounds, as the instructions allow. The report lists them.

**One gap left, filed as `DX-bug-globs-unnamed-inherit`:**
- If the bug text names no file, or names only extensionless files such as `Dockerfile`, the fix task still inherits all the source globs. Existing tests pin that fallback, and changing it needs a decision. The critic raised it twice; I refuted it both times with that explanation.

**Procedure note:**
- `ddflow_identify` rejected `name` (its argument is `agent`), so I passed `--agent fleet-fixes-a` on every CLI call instead.

1. Run `ddflow claim DX-health-watch --force`.
2. Commit the 7 files.
3. Merge main into the branch.

**fix-upgrade-written-digest-ignores-git-filters**
- `digests()` in `ddflow/services/upgrade_written.py` now records the blob id git would store, from `git hash-object --path`, through the shared `infra.git` interface. It falls back to SHA-256 if git can't answer.

- The `claim --resources gpu=1` bypass came from roborev job 2906. It was reproduced and fixed in `acquire` in `ddflow/services/leases.py`.
- The regression test is `tests/test_resources.py::test_a_capacity_style_spec_is_refused_not_stored_as_a_name`. It covers `task add`, `update` and `claim`.

data.body: ddflow cannot push to a running agent, but every agent already calls ddflow regularly and runs hooks. Compute drift = commits on the base since the branch's merge base, split into RELEVANT (touch the item's globs, its pin files, the files its diff changed, or add/supersede a decision governing them) and unrelated. Surface it as one line on: heartbeat/lease renew replies, `ddflow brief`, gate_status, and the UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse hook context (once per change of base sha, not every call): 'main moved: 14 commits, 3 touch your files (ddflow/services/ci.py ...); run ddflow sync'. Knobs [sync].notify = off|relevant|all, [sync].relevant_commits (default 1), [sync].block_commits for the claim/merge side. For each: use target_branch(it, cfg, default, line) (or the recorded item.base) for behind-counts, scratch merges in ci, enforce's behind check (max_behind compares against the branch the work merges into), pins merge driver, merge queue, reports ('differs from main'), cleanup, recall tests. Add an architecture guard that counts literal 'main'/'master' and bare default_branch uses outside core/flow.py with a ratchet baseline. Regression: a gitflow repo where main is far ahead of develop must not warn 'behind'. (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)
data.title: Audit and guard: nothing branch-relative assumes main; everything uses the item's recorded base

data.body: A strategy declares, in TOML with a packaged default each: base per item class (feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, docs), merge target(s) and back-merge targets, branch naming, whether integration is merge or PR, how versions/tags are cut, which branches are protected, and the drift base. Built on the registry (P-extension-seams.registry). trunk and gitflow keep their behaviour exactly ([flow].model stays as an alias per D-compat); github-flow (short-lived branches from main, PR, deploy from main), version-line (long-lived release/x.y with backports and forward merges), release-train (periodic cut from develop) are added; an operator-written strategy drops into .ddflow/conf.d/. Per project, per line, per phase override. (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)
data.title: Branching strategies as data: trunk, github-flow, gitflow, version lines, release-train, custom TOML

data.body: For big features that must not touch main until done. [flow].phase_branches = off|opt-in|all; a phase tagged branch:own gets an integration branch cut from the parent base; every task of the phase records that branch as its base (so drift, ci scratch merges and merge all follow it), the branch is kept synced to its parent on the DX-sync-points cadence, and closing the phase runs the phase-end full suite and phase review (D-phase-review-r2) on the branch, then lands it on the parent by the strategy's rule (merge or PR). Nested phases stack. Abandoning the phase abandons the branch only on request. (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)
data.title: Phase/epic integration branches: a phase owns phase/P-x; its tasks branch from and land on it; the phase lands on its parent at phase end

data.body: From the repo: default branch, presence of develop/release/hotfix branches, tags, protected-branch rules (forge CLI when present), merge-commit vs squash history, CODEOWNERS/PR templates. Propose the closest strategy with the evidence, never apply silently (the operator accepts); doctor warns when the configured strategy and the repo disagree (e.g. gitflow configured but no develop branch). (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)
data.title: Onboarding detects the repo's branching strategy and proposes the [flow] config; doctor checks it still matches

data.body: For every packaged strategy a scenario against a throwaway git repo: claim, drift when the base moves, sync, merge, hotfix back-merge, backport across lines, stacked tasks retargeting when the lower task lands, phase branch land, PR mode with a fake forge. The same scenarios run as `ddflow flow check` against a project's own config with a dry-run repo clone so an operator can verify a custom strategy before using it. Lives in the integration_tests set (not item-level). (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)
data.title: Real-git scenario suite per strategy plus `ddflow flow check`

data.body: port-of exists for filing the port task. Add the ledger: when an item lands on a maintenance line, ddflow records the owed forward merges per the strategy (1.2 -> 1.3 -> develop/main), shows them in brief/doctor until each is merged or consciously declined, and `ddflow sync` of a line branch offers the forward merge. Conflicts become tasks, not silent drops. (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)

<result>Report: `/tmp/claude-1001/research/coderabbit.md`. Nothing else was written or changed.

Top 8 ideas, ranked:
1. Review learnings. A refuted finding becomes a probe-backed, expiring note that is delivered to later reviews and pre-marks identical re-raises.
2. Finding confidence plus a `[review].profile` / `fail_floor` knob. Findings below the floor are advisory.
3. `ddflow metrics review`: per reviewer, gate and severity precision, taken from triage verdicts.
4. Natural-language `check` records with a passed / failed / inconclusive verdict, hooked into the standards gate.
5. A `FIX:` field on findings plus a `review findings --agent` NDJSON feed, with an optional apply-check in a scratch worktree.
6. An advisory automatic finding verifier (off by default).
7. Diff-scoped tool findings, secret scan first, fed to the reviewer as pre-pass context.
8. A derived merge-readiness verdict with a coverage-based confidence.

The report also covers ideas 9 to 12 (docstring ratchet, TODO capture at merge, maintainability lens, receipt walkthrough), the rejected list, and an unfiled phase `P-review-quality` with 21 tasks.

Could not verify:
- CodeRabbit's internal verification and filtering, the models it uses, and any "code graph" feature. The docs are silent on all three.
- The Martian benchmark numbers and the 270-vs-70 false-positive tally. They come from search summaries; morphllm.com returned HTTP 429.
- Pricing tiers for each feature, and how the walkthrough updates on later commits.
- Whether ddflow's `BL-structural` phase overlaps ast-grep rules. I did not open it.
- Token and time costs in the report are my estimates, not measurements.

`ddflow similar` scored below its threshold for every phrase I tried. I checked overlap by grepping the full task list instead.</result>

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-17: lessons must stay current; end-of-item updating. P-lessons.obligation covers only bugs and only warns. Extend to every item: at `complete` (and in `ddflow report`), ddflow scans the item's event trail for surprise signals: a review round forced past its budget, a gate skipped/forced/recorded by hand or unavailable, baseline-red, a bug found or filed during the item, more than one merge attempt, a fix round with confirmed findings in one category, a lease broken or lapsed, a test reopened. It drafts 1-3 candidate lessons (title, rule, why from the evidence, scope globs from the item's files, pattern if a finding names one) and shows them; the agent picks with `ddflow lesson add --from-item ITEM --pick N` or declines with `--no-lesson --reason`. Knob lessons.require_on_surprise = off|warn|block (default warn); the reason is logged. No LLM call needed for the draft (templates over the evidence); a cheap role may polish. Reuses lessons.auto_capture_on_bug.
data.title: At complete, draft lesson candidates from the item's own evidence and require a lesson or a reason when there was a surprise

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-17. Today's coordinator session recorded no lesson for three days although it hit a dozen surprises (priority scale, list truncation, contested decisions, load): the rule 'a lesson after any surprise' was a request, not a step. At `ddflow session end` (and the SessionEnd/Stop hook, and when the agent brief says stop) ddflow lists the session's notes, prompts that were corrections, bugs found, forced/skipped gates and decisions changed, drafts candidate lessons from them (same drafter as PL-capture-candidates) and asks for record-or-decline; a session with corrections and no lesson prints a one-line warning in the next `ddflow brief`. Knob lessons.session_end = off|prompt|warn.
data.title: Session end and coordinator duty: surface unrecorded surprises and the operator's corrections as lesson candidates

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-17: always up to date. A lesson names paths, commands, config keys, decision ids and test names. Check them cheaply (incrementally, on the files a change touches, via P-lessons.checks): path missing or moved (git log --follow), command or flag no longer in the CLI tables, knob gone, governing decision superseded, pattern no longer matches anywhere. A failing check marks the lesson `stale` with the reason (not deleted); the brief shows 'maybe stale: reason' instead of hiding it; ddflow lessons curate (P-lessons.curate) proposes retire, rewrite or re-scope; the periodic roadmap_review pass runs the check. Shares the drift calculation with RR-freshness (task-vs-repo) and DX-drift-notice.
data.title: Lessons go stale mechanically: verify the files, commands and decisions a lesson names, mark it stale, surface it in the brief and the curate pass

data.body:
Today lessons reach the agent only through the brief's text ranking (max 5). Add the glob-scoped lessons for the item's files to the claim guidance and to the dispatch brief (P-safeguards.dispatch), and the relevant ones to the rubber_duck and critic gate prompts, all through the shared relevance engine and budget; record guidance.delivered with lesson ids so recurrence can tell 'delivered and repeated' from 'never delivered'.

START OF ITEM (operator question 2026-10-17, teach at the beginning): the `rules` gate (first gate) prints the lessons that apply to the item's files and records which were delivered (guidance.delivered); its research note must say 'applies' or 'not applicable' for any lesson flagged as recurring (P-lessons.recurrence), so a repeated mistake is either a delivered-and-ignored lesson or a never-delivered one. The end-of-item half is PL-capture-candidates; the session half PL-session-end; staleness PL-staleness.

data.body: setup/onboard detect: git worktrees in use, pytest and xdist, LLM reviewers configured, multiple agents, the languages (SC-onboard stack proposal). Offer the matching packs in the one onboarding conversation, showing entry titles and counts; ddflow-usage and multi-agent-git are offered by default, others when their applies_when matches. Install is opt-in per pack (consent, D-fallback-no-remote style: nothing silent), creates records with origin pack:<name>@<version> and trust ddflow, excluded from the project's lesson counts and curate proposals unless adopted (`ddflow packs adopt ENTRY` copies it into the project's own lessons). `ddflow packs install|remove|list|diff`. Also callable later (existing projects: doctor notes 'packs not offered').
data.title: Offer the packs when a project is bootstrapped: setup, onboard and adopt detect the stack and offer matching packs, opt-in, kept apart from the project's own lessons

data.body: `ddflow upgrade` plans pack changes next to its other writes: new entries (offered, not auto-enabled if the pack is opt-in per entry), changed entries (diff shown; a project that edited its copy keeps its edit as an override layer and sees the upstream diff), retired entries (marked retired_in, shown as stale, removed on accept). A declined entry stays declined across versions (decline memory). Provenance kept (origin pack:name@version). Uses the upgrade machinery (B-upgrade, done) and managed-region semantics.
data.title: Keep installed packs current through ddflow upgrade: new, changed and retired entries as a plan; project edits and declines are preserved

data.body: `ddflow improve --lesson ID` (D-continuous-improvement route: into a ddflow source checkout's queue, never push or PR; otherwise a GitHub report with the operator's acceptance) turns a project lesson into a pack candidate: strips project paths, names, ids and secrets (sensitivity scan, SE-sensitivity), rewrites ddflow-internal references, proposes the pack and applies_when, and shows the operator exactly what would leave the machine before anything is sent. Recurring lessons across several projects (when ddflow can see more than one) rank higher. Accepted candidates become pack entries via LP-seed's curation path.
data.title: Feed packs from projects: promote a project's own lesson into an upstream candidate with redaction and operator consent

data.body: Per pack entry: how often delivered (guidance.delivered), how often a recurrence matched it (lesson.recurred), refuted/ignored counts, token cost; `ddflow packs report` and a periodic pass that proposes retiring entries never delivered or never matched in N days across installs of this project, and entries whose recurrence stays high after delivery (the wording is not working). Uses P-lessons.effect; per-project, never phoned home.
data.title: Measure each pack entry: delivered, matched, repeated; retire the ones that never help

data.body: Fake project and fake ddflow versions; checks opt-in consent, record origin and trust, override layer after an edit, decline memory, redaction output, and the effect report. Part of the integration set.
data.title: Acceptance: a fresh project bootstrapped with ddflow gets the offered packs, an upgrade changes one entry and retires another, a declined entry stays declined, a project lesson becomes a redacted upstream candidate

Operator questions:
- (a) Agent-native research and deep research: NOT COVERED. Nothing in the ddflow code or the 22 harness descriptors mentions web search or deep research, and descriptor-v2 reserves no section for it.
- (b) Multi-model checking and other techniques: PARTLY. B-rw-verify, RF-confidence and the replicate flow (RF-flows-core) cover other-family verification. B-pi-review-panel gives agreement counts but only for code review. There is no research-claim panel, agreement scoring or disagreement resolution.
- (c) Research critic: PARTLY. B-rw-verify has a refute pass and RF-roles has a skeptic lens. There is no report-level critic with a rubric.

Top 8 ideas, in rank order:
1. Add a `[research]` section to the descriptor (search tools, modes, enable flag, limits, deep-research adapter), amended in through the descriptor-v2 owner.
2. Add a web/consent/spend policy knob that passes the right flags to the harness.
3. Add a delegated deep-research lane through APIs (OpenAI, Gemini with `collaborative_planning`, Perplexity). It needs consent, cost preview and budget, and a delegated report enters at "asserted".
4. Add a multi-family claim panel that scores agreement by family and resolves contested claims from evidence, built on B-pi-review-panel.
5. Extend the citation audit to check statement support (does the cited span back the claim) and whether the cited URL was ever fetched.
6. Add a provenance trace record per search, fetch or delegated call.
7. Add a report-level research critic lens with a rubric, one adversarial round, other family.
8. Add effort-scaling and budget rules from Anthropic's multi-agent write-up, passed through as `max_uses` / `max_tool_calls`.
(Ideas 9 and 10, MCP search companions and a rubric-scored report eval, are in the report along with the rejected ideas and an 11-task proposed list.)

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-18: should ddflow automate the stale checks? Yes. Seen all day: agents report 'waiting on the review/ci/pins' for 15 to 60 minutes after the background process they started died, was killed, or finished and its monitor was lost (fleet-dx-l, fleet-bugs2, fleet-unblock-b). DX-health-watch detects idle, stalled, unresponsive, locked, crashed and runaway lanes, but it cannot tell a LEGITIMATE long wait (a DeepSeek review of 15-30 minutes) from a DEAD one, so it either nudges the legitimate waits or misses the dead ones. Needs one fact: the live-run registry (services/gates/running.py, shared with DX-gate-run-same-commit-live, DX-review-concurrent-runs and DX-gate-run-detach): every gate/review/ci/pins run records item, gate, pid, start time, log path and expected duration; the finish records the outcome. New finding ORPHAN_WAIT: a lane with no progress for [health].orphan_s (default 300) whose newest registry entry is finished or whose pid is gone with no recorded outcome: 'DX-x waits on review rubber_duck: run 4412 ended 12 min ago (outcome recorded: passed, see ddflow gate status) / died with no outcome (log: ...); rerun: ddflow review DX-x --gate rubber_duck'. The opposite check: a lane whose registered run is alive and within its expected duration is NOT idle or stalled (no nudge). The correction ladder is the existing one (nudge, then stop request); the nudge text and the heartbeat reply carry the finding so the agent itself sees it. Also exposed in ddflow lanes and ddflow health.
data.title: Health watch: a lane that is waiting on a gate, review, ci or pins run whose process is gone (or never started) is 'waiting on nothing': say so, name the log and the command to rerun

<result>Report: `/tmp/claude-1001/research/history-collapse-extract.md`. I changed nothing in the repo.

- **(A) Collapse: feasible, but the sha handling is the hard part.** `D-log-in-main-tree` keeps the log as plain files in the tree. The tip tree already holds all 78k events, so a squash loses no event. What it loses is every recorded sha as an ancestor, other clones' positions, and branches and tags based on old commits. A local experiment on git 2.43.0 showed the old sha still resolves via an archive ref but is not an ancestor. A default `git clone` fetched neither `refs/archive/*` nor `refs/replace/*`.
- **(B) Extract/regenerate: partly, needs prerequisites.**
  - **What transfers mechanically:** the queue, decisions, rules, lessons, research and rendered docs.
  - **What does not:** source code is not in the log. Regeneration means new agent implementations against the old tests and fixtures.
  - **Prerequisites:** blobs in the bundle (`B-logscale-blob-backup`), sensitivity labels on all record families (`SE-sensitivity-doors`), and structured acceptance fields. Acceptance is free text in task bodies today.

Top 6 ideas:
1. Write a verified `git bundle` of the repo plus `.ddflow/blobs` (`archive bundle`). It is safe on its own and covers the `B-gap-log-backup` recipe.
2. Add a shared `resolve_sha` plus a `history.rewritten` event whose old-to-new map lives in a blob. The log stays unmodified.
3. Run `collapse plan` as a dry run with blocker checks first. Then `apply` by phase or range, operator-only, with a bundle, archive ref and tag, and nothing pushed.
4. Prove equivalence: `.ddflow/` identical across the old and new tips, plus a new folded-State digest for `replay --verify-state`. Today `replay --verify` only checks sha resolution.
5. `extract` and `seed` in records mode, with a sensitivity ceiling, prompts opt-in, an optional oracle pack, tasks reopened and the other records imported with provenance. Reuse the LP, SDD and KB-layer formats.
6. Do events-only squash and log compaction last. No kind is declared `compact` today, and `lease.renewed` is 40% of events.

Operator decisions needed:
1. The goal: smaller history, smaller clone, or tidier history.
2. Which archive survives, and what happens to release tags.
3. Which collapse forms are allowed, and whether only the operator may apply.
4. Whether other clones and open PRs are a hard refusal.
5. For extract: the sensitivity ceiling, whether prompts are included, whether tests and fixtures go in the bundle, and whether imported records stay in a separate layer.
